size_rationale: Small because it is a one-line fix in one file, and the prompt names the leaking field (password), whose definition in the user model is the place; confirming the option name means a glance at the toJSON plugin, two files at most.
prompt: User objects in API responses now include the hashed `password` field, for example the `user` returned by POST /v1/auth/register and POST /v1/auth/login, and GET /v1/users/:userId.

root_cause.detail: The password field is marked `hidden: true` instead of `private: true`; the toJSON plugin only strips paths whose options have `private`, so the hash is serialized.

fail_to_pass: tests/unit/models/user.model.test.js > User model > User toJSON() > should not return user password when toJSON is called
tests/integration/auth.test.js > Auth routes > POST /v1/auth/register > should return 201 and successfully register user if request data is ok
oracle.cmd: npx jest tests/unit/models/user.model.test.js tests/integration/auth.test.js -t 'should not return user password when toJSON is called|should return 201 and successfully register user if request data is ok'
